text:
Maya: Quick heads-up — after the eu-west1 preemptible rotation this morning we saw a measurable bump in streaming requeues and a few tail-latency spikes (~150-300ms). Requeues up ~2.7%.
Liam: Do you know whether this was a single pool griefing or broad preempt churn?
Maya: Mixed-capacity pools mostly. On-demand stayed stable; preemptible tranche evaporated quickly and the LB terminated connections before runtimes could hand off session state.
Raj: Can you paste a sanitized log snippet so I can triage replay behavior?
Maya: Sure — router/runtime excerpts:
```
[router] 2026-04-02T08:12:34Z node=eu-gw-3 action=terminate reason=preempt_notice
[runtime] 2026-04-02T08:12:34Z session=ses-77f state=emit_resume_token token=rtk-9a prefix=kv-ptr-77f
[worker] 2026-04-02T08:12:34Z req=stream-456 action=requeue->queue=standby
```
Sofia: Looks like runtime produces a resume token but LB RST/FIN closes the socket too soon. Clients drop before they can reconnect.
Liam: So two failure modes: LB-level aggressive TCP teardown, and slow replication of the minimal session checkpoint from primary -> standby.
Maya: Proposal sketch for mitigation:
  - Node labeling: mark nodes label=preemptible=true so infra can treat them specially.
  - LB change: for nodes with label=preemptible=true set connectionDraining window=30s and advertise header x-resume-drain:1 for new connections.
  - Fast checkpoint: on preempt notice, runtime writes a compact session checkpoint (checkpoint={session_id, kv_pointer, last_token_offset}) to the control plane with a 200ms SLO.
  - Short-lived resume token: runtime emits a region-bound resume token valid 8s, used only by same-region standby runtimes.
  - Resume idempotency: resume accepted only if resume_offset > persisted_committed_offset.
  - Session-length heuristic: if session_age < 1s prefer simple requeue rather than checkpointing to avoid write storms.
Sofia: Agree. For the LB changes, we should scope to preemptible nodes only. Example config snippet (pseudo):
```
backendServices:
  - name: eu-preemptible-backend
    connectionDraining:
      drainingTimeoutSec: 30
    headers:
      - name: x-resume-drain
        value: "1"
```
Raj: Concern: mass preempt could cause tons of checkpoint writes and overwhelm etcd/control-plane. How to prevent write amplification?
Maya: Ideas to mitigate write pressure:
  - Aggregate checkpoint updates into 100ms buckets and coalesce per session.
  - Backpressure with jittered windowing: prioritize oldest sessions for immediate flush, delay tiny sessions.
  - If checkpoint write fails or latency exceeds threshold, fall back to queue-based requeue and mark metric "resume_path_degraded".
Liam: Also need idempotency reasoning to avoid double-execution: use (session_id, last_offset, resume_nonce). Runtime should ignore a resume if its resume_offset <= committed_offset.
Sofia: Observability additions:
  - preempt_notice_count{zone}
  - session_checkpoint_write_latency_p50_p95
  - resume_token_issue_count
  - resume_success_rate
  - requeues_per_preempt
Maya: Operational plan / rollout:
  1) infra: add node label support + LB draining rule scoping (staged change)
  2) runtime: add compact checkpoint write path + resume token logic + idempotency checks
  3) canary: enable new runtime on 10% of preemptible pool in eu-west1, monitor for 2 hours
  4) expand to 50% then 100% if metrics look good
Raj: For older runtime versions that can't checkpoint: rollout can rely on hybrid pools where only labeled preemptible nodes get the longer drain and new runtime. Others stay with existing short drain and requeue behavior.
Liam: Also add a circuit-breaker in control plane: if preempt_notice_count in zone spikes > X within Y, temporarily raise checkpoint aggregation window to avoid overload.
Maya: Good call. Quick TODOs:
  - @Raj: small PR for idempotency checks + resume_nonce handling
  - @Sofia: update dashboards + add alert: resume_success_rate < 98% for 15m -> page
  - @Liam: infra change to LB draining rule (staged rollout)
  - @Maya: draft RFC with config diffs and canary timeline
infra-bot: RFC created: RFC-2060-resume-handback (https://rfd/redwood/rfc-2060)
oncall-bot: Alerting rule added: resume_success_rate < 98% for 15m -> pager duty
Sofia: One more note: for multi-tenant cost leakage, ensure resume tokens are constrained to the same-customer and same-region; reject cross-region resumes to avoid cross-zone egress.
Raj: Also include metric tagging by node_label=preemptible for easy filtering.
Maya: Can we start the canary tomorrow 09:00 UTC?
Liam: I'm good with that timeline.
Raj: SGTM.
Sofia: +1 :thumbsup:
Maya: Thanks — I'll post the RFC link and hook up a canary dashboard when the infra change is staged.
